reason: Independently re-measured every cited org-config datum on the live FortraUAT org 2026-06-30; all match the executor's FAIL row exactly. This is a config-query scenario, not a DML fixture, so the default TEST-DATA-ARTIFACT hypothesis (malformed seed / headless $0 / inactive PBE) is structurally inapplicable -- there is no fixture, no priced line, no Apex insert. The cited org-config state is REAL and CURRENT: 6 of 11 non-USD CurrencyType.ConversionRate values sit at placeholder 1.0, and DatedConversionRate (Advanced Currency Mgmt ON) reset those same currencies to 1.0 from 2026-02-11, so any foreign transaction dated >= 2026-02-11 consolidates foreign->USD at face value across reports/dashboards/DocGen/Workday invoicing. A real user running a multi-currency report or generating a DocGen FX-converted document WOULD hit this (uiUserWouldHit=yes), so it is a genuine ORG-CONFIG-DEFECT (SC-3384), not an artifact and not an expectation error. The executor was disciplined: it did NOT mislabel this a PROCEDURE-DEFECT -- it explicitly confirmed V21 is CLEAN because the proc reads Currency_Conversion_Formula__mdt (re-verified: all 10 rates correct and active) rather than CurrencyType, corroborated by G-01 EUR 500->467.3 (x0.9346 mdt, not x0.92 CurrencyType). branchConfirmedFired=false because no V21 branch is involved -- the defect surface is the reporting/DocGen/invoicing engines downstream of CurrencyType, by design outside the priced-line path. Authoritative expected rates are sourced from the Confluence ARR table and corroborated by the mdt, so the expected value is not itself wrong. Conclusion: the FAIL stands as a real ORG-CONFIG-DEFECT; I agree with the executor.
